fixes.explanation: Baal is it. Hosea 13:1 says Ephraim was exalted in Israel, “But he incurred guilt through Baal, and he died.” When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling. I think that's a sobering turn.

True. Hosea 13:2 says the idols are made skillfully from their silver, “…all of them the work of craftsmen.” So these weren't rough lumps of metal. A lot of careful work went into them, and the text calls the making of them sin.

They vanish. Morning mist, early dew that vanishes, chaff blown from a threshing floor, and smoke through an open window all pass away (Hosea 13:3). The LORD says that's what the idol makers will be like. Four pictures, one message, and nobody can say it didn't get through.

Wilderness. The LORD says, “I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.” (Hosea 13:5) He says He is the LORD their God ever since the land of Egypt (Hosea 13:4). Dry land, and He knew them there.

The fox doesn't show up in these verses. Hosea 13:8 says, “Like a bear robbed of her cubs I will attack them…” The animals named are a lion, a leopard and a bear, plus a wild beast tearing them apart. The bear is the one to remember.
The neighbors don't come up in this verse at all. Hosea 13:9 gives the reason: “…because you are against Me…” and He calls Himself their helper. This one is about Israel and the LORD.

The text says something very different. Hosea 13:11 says, “So in My anger I gave you a king, and in My wrath I took him away.” The king came in anger, not as a reward. The people had asked, “Give me a king and princes…” (Hosea 13:10).

Yes, a promise right in the middle of the warnings. The LORD says, “I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from Death.” (Hosea 13:14) Ransom and redeem are big words. That's a big promise, so hold onto it.

The king isn't the one sending this wind. Hosea 13:15 says it is “…a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert.” Verse 10 asked where the king was to save them. The wind comes from the LORD, not from the king.
True. Hosea 13:15 says, “An east wind will come…” and then, “His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry.” Ephraim may flourish among his brothers, but the LORD says this is coming.

The text says it will. Hosea 13:15 says, “His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry.” Ephraim may flourish among his brothers, but the verse goes on to say his fountain fails and his treasury is plundered.
Sheep aren't named in this verse. Hosea 13:15 says, “The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.” It's the treasury that gets plundered. Flocks aren't on the list.

That's the reason given. Hosea 13:16 says, “Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God.” The rest of that verse is very heavy. Rebellion against her God is the reason it states.
Tribute isn't mentioned in this verse. Hosea 13:16 says, “Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God.” The reason the text gives is rebellion against her God.
The prophets aren't mentioned in this verse. Hosea 13:16 says, “Samaria will bear her guilt because she has rebelled against her God.” Rebellion against her God is the reason the verse gives.
